title: Imports and Setup
content: Imports Nat.GCD.Basic (for LCM), Finset.Basic, Real.Basic, Real.log, and BigOperators (for Σ notation). Opens Nat, Real, Finset, and BigOperators namespaces. All work is in the Erdos856 namespace.
mathContext: Uses `Nat.lcm` for $\text{lcm}(a,b)$, `Real.log` for $\log x$, and `∑ n ∈ A, f(n)` for $\sum_{n \in A} f(n)$.

title: LCM Definition and Properties (PROVED)
content: Defines myLcm as Nat.lcm wrapper, then proves commutativity lcm(a,b) = lcm(b,a) and idempotence lcm(a,a) = a. Both are one-line proofs delegating to Nat.lcm_comm and Nat.lcm_self.
mathContext: $\text{lcm}(a,b) = ab / \gcd(a,b)$. Properties: $\text{lcm}(a,b) = \text{lcm}(b,a)$, $\text{lcm}(a,a) = a$. These are genuine Lean proofs.

title: Uniform Pairwise LCM
content: HasUniformPairwiseLCM A t requires that for all distinct a, b ∈ A, lcm(a,b) = t. This is the forbidden structure: a k-element set where every pair has the same LCM. Such sets arise naturally among divisors of t.
mathContext: $\text{HasUniformPairwiseLCM}(A, t) \equiv \forall a, b \in A,\, a \neq b \Rightarrow \text{lcm}(a, b) = t$. Example: $\{2, 3, 6\}$ has uniform LCM $6$.

title: k-LCM-Free Set
content: IsLCMFree A k means A contains no k-element subset with uniform pairwise LCM. This is the avoidance condition: we maximize harmonic sum subject to no k elements sharing a common LCM pattern.
mathContext: $\text{IsLCMFree}(A, k) \equiv \neg \exists B \subseteq A,\, |B| = k \land \exists t,\, \text{HasUniformPairwiseLCM}(B, t)$.

title: Harmonic Sum
content: harmonicSum A = Σ_{n∈A} 1/n, with a guard for n = 0 (maps to 0). This measures logarithmic density: for the full set {1,...,N}, the harmonic sum is ~log N. The problem asks how close to log N the sum can get while avoiding LCM patterns.
mathContext: $\text{harmonicSum}(A) = \sum_{n \in A} \frac{1}{n}$. For $A = \{1, \ldots, N\}$: $\sum_{n=1}^N 1/n = \ln N + \gamma + O(1/N)$ where $\gamma \approx 0.5772$ is Euler's constant.

title: The Extremal Function f_k(N)
content: f_k(k, N) = sup{harmonicSum(A) : A ⊆ {1,...,N}, IsLCMFree A k}. Defined via sSup over the set of achievable harmonic sums. This is the central quantity — known to be Θ((log N)^{c_k}) for some c_k ∈ (0, 1].
mathContext: $f_k(N) = \sup\left\{\sum_{n \in A} \frac{1}{n} : A \subseteq [N],\, \text{IsLCMFree}(A, k)\right\}$. Growth rate: $(\log N)^{b_k} \leq f_k(N) \leq (\log N)^{c_k}$.

title: Erdős 1970 Upper Bound
content: Axiomatizes Erdős's bound f_k(N) ≤ C · log(N)/log(log(N)). The proof idea: for each t, the number of a ∈ A with t = ap for some prime p is < k (else k elements have uniform LCM = t). Summing over primes gives the bound. Also axiomatizes the key prime factorization lemma.
mathContext: $f_k(N) \leq C \cdot \frac{\log N}{\log\log N}$. Key lemma: $|\{a \in A : \exists p \text{ prime},\, t = ap\}| < k$ for each $t$, since otherwise $k$ elements of $A$ have $\text{lcm} = t$.

title: Tang–Zhang 2025 Bounds
content: Axiomatizes the Tang–Zhang improvement: there exist constants 0 < b_k ≤ c_k ≤ 1 such that for all ε > 0, eventually (log N)^{b_k - ε} ≤ f_k(N) ≤ (log N)^{c_k + ε}. This replaces Erdős's log/loglog bound with power-of-log bounds.
mathContext: $\forall \varepsilon > 0,\, \exists N_0: \forall N \geq N_0,\, (\log N)^{b_k - \varepsilon} \leq f_k(N) \leq (\log N)^{c_k + \varepsilon}$. For $k = 3$: $b_3 \geq 0.438$, $c_3 \leq 0.889$.

title: k = 3 Explicit Bounds
content: Specific exponents for the most studied case k = 3: (log N)^{0.438} ≤ f_3(N) ≤ (log N)^{0.889}. The gap between 0.438 and 0.889 leaves the true exponent c_3 undetermined.
mathContext: For $k = 3$: $(\log N)^{0.438} \leq f_3(N) \leq (\log N)^{0.889}$. The ratio $0.889/0.438 \approx 2.03$ shows the bounds are off by a factor of $\sim 2$ in the exponent.

title: Sunflower and Sunflower Conjecture
content: Defines k-sunflowers (k sets where every distinct pair has the same intersection, the 'core') and the sunflower conjecture for k: any family of sets each of size ≤ s contains a k-sunflower if the family has > (ck)^s members. The Erdős–Rado sunflower lemma (1960) gives (k-1)^s · s!, and the conjecture improves this to polynomial in k.
mathContext: $\text{IsSunflower}(\mathcal{F}, k) \equiv |\mathcal{F}| = k \land \exists C,\, \forall S \neq T \in \mathcal{F},\, S \cap T = C$. Conjecture: $|\mathcal{F}| > (ck)^s \Rightarrow \exists k\text{-sunflower} \subseteq \mathcal{F}$.

title: Sunflower Equivalence
content: Axiomatizes the deep equivalence: c_k < 1 (non-trivial upper bound on f_k(N)) if and only if the sunflower conjecture holds for k-petalled sunflowers. This connects a number-theoretic extremal problem to a purely combinatorial conjecture.
mathContext: $\text{SunflowerConjectureForK}(k) \iff \exists c_k < 1: f_k(N) \leq (\log N)^{c_k + o(1)}$. The forward direction uses LCM structure to build sunflowers; the reverse uses sunflower-free families to build LCM-free sets.

title: Natural Density Variant
content: Defines g_k(N) = max|A| over k-LCM-free subsets (natural density instead of harmonic sum). Axiomatizes g_4(N) ≫ N and g_3(N) ≫ N: sets of linear size can avoid the LCM condition. The harmonic sum version is the harder and more interesting quantity.
mathContext: $g_k(N) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq [N],\, \text{IsLCMFree}(A, k)\}$. For $k \geq 3$: $g_k(N) \geq CN$ for some $C > 0$. The harmonic sum $f_k(N)$ is much smaller: $f_k(N) \leq (\log N)^{c_k}$.

title: Divisor Set LCM Property (PROVED)
content: Proves that if a, b both divide n, then lcm(a,b) divides n. This is a genuine Lean proof using Nat.lcm_dvd_iff. It shows divisor sets naturally have LCM structure, motivating the avoidance condition.
mathContext: $a \mid n \land b \mid n \Rightarrow \text{lcm}(a, b) \mid n$. Proof: $\text{lcm}(a,b) \mid n \iff a \mid n \land b \mid n$ (`Nat.lcm_dvd_iff`).

title: Open Problem and Gap Analysis
content: Formalizes the open problem: does there exist a unique c_k such that f_k(N) = (log N)^{c_k ± o(1)}? The gap analysis for k = 3 shows exponents between 0.438 and 0.889 — the true value is unknown.
mathContext: Open: $\exists! c_k: \forall \varepsilon > 0,\, (\log N)^{c_k - \varepsilon} \leq f_k(N) \leq (\log N)^{c_k + \varepsilon}$ eventually. For $k = 3$: $0.438 \leq c_3 \leq 0.889$.
